subject: Clarify MSA: output ownership, training permissions, and evidence list
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@asterlabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.legal@asterlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on MSA terms (output + training)

Jordan — thanks for the draft MSA and order form. We reviewed with legal and have two main asks that will block internal approval: 

1) Output ownership / productization: we need clarity that outputs generated by your hosted API using our confidential prompts/data will not be used by Redwood to train models or be sold as part of other products. We understand redlines around an "evaluation/telemetry" exception — please confirm the scope.

2) Feedback/data license: your order form currently grants a broad feedback license back to Redwood. We need this limited to aggregated, anonymized telemetry and explicitly exclude any verbatim customer content.

Attached is a short list of requested redline snippets (aster_requested_redlines.pdf) and an internal approval checklist. We can do a quick call if helpful — Sara and I are available early next week.

Thanks,
Mike
--
Mike Turner
Head of Platform Partnerships
Aster Labs
attachment: aster_requested_redlines.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA terms (output + training)

Mike — appreciate the clear asks and the PDF. Short answer: we can make two actionable proposals that map to your checklist.

Proposal A (default for hosted API customers):
- Redwood will not use customer prompts or verbatim outputs to train base models without explicit opt-in.
- We will retain telemetry (latency, token counts, aggregated failure rates) for ops and product improvement; no verbatim output retention for training.

Proposal B (opt-in managed training):
- Customer may grant a narrow training license for a defined dataset for agreed purposes; this would be an add-on in the order form with associated data handling controls.

On the feedback license: we can carve out a clause that excludes customer confidential content and limits the license to non-identifiable aggregated signals and model performance feedback.

Laura — can you scope procurement implications and the discounting/terms impact if Aster wants Proposal B as an add-on? Karthik — would appreciate a legal redline we can send back that includes the two carveouts (no training w/o opt-in; feedback license limited to aggregated telemetry).

I attached the order form draft with the Aster line items and a first pass (JBL-orderform-draft.docx). If acceptable, we can route via DocuSign and get procurement signoff next week.

Thanks,
Jordan
--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachment: JBL-orderform-draft.docx (DOCX, 22KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Turner <mike.turner@asterlabs.com>, Sara Lee <sara.legal@asterlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA terms (output + training)

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 10:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — appreciate the clear asks and the PDF. Short answer: we can make two actionable proposals...

Thanks for the summary. Quick legal read: the language Jordan suggests is workable, but we should be explicit in three places to avoid interpretive gaps:

1) Define "verbatim customer content" and list examples (prompts, files uploaded, PII-containing outputs) — keep definition narrow but concrete.
2) Telemetry carveout: allow collection of aggregated metrics and non-reversible hashes for debugging; prohibit storage of full outputs for training without a separate Data Processing Annex (DPA) and written opt-in.
3) Feedback license: convert to a "nonexclusive, nontransferable right to use anonymized signals" and prohibit use of any content identified as confidential under the MSA.

Action items: I'll prepare a redline of the MSA + Order Form with the three bullets implemented. I will:
- Inline-edit the MSA Section 4.2 (Data & Use) with a training opt-in flow, and add an exhibit for the add-on training scope.
- Add a brief evidence checklist for procurement: proof of data deletion policy, KMS/HSM keying details for customer data, SOC 2 artifact pointer.

Jordan/Laura — expect the redline by EOD Monday. Mike/Sara — once we have their internal approvals, we should plan a 30-min alignment call (legal + procurement) to agree exact wording.

Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Mike / Sara — looping back to confirm next steps and timing after Karthik's note.

Planned timeline: 
- Monday EOD (PST): Karthik sends redline MSA + Order Form with explicit carveouts and an exhibit for any training opt-in.
- Within 24 hours of redline: Aster legal to confirm whether Proposal A is sufficient or if they will request Proposal B (training add-on).
- If Proposal B: procurement evidence list (SOC 2 + KMS details) required before we enable managed training; Laura, please confirm any procurement gating and lead time for additional approval.

Next step: I'll schedule a 30-min call for Monday 3:30pm PT with Karthik + Laura + Mike + Sara to walk through redlines. If that slot doesn't work I will propose an alternate. DocuSign link will be generated once redlines are accepted (see related link).
